stepNotes.1: The unit exposes IconProps and a memoized Icon component from Icon.tsx, projects IconName directly from the generated sprite keys, and exports the 227-entry iconSpriteData constant.
stepNotes.2: sprite.ts is generated from the installed Remixicon bundle; inspection found 227 non-empty, path-only entries with no duplicate keys, and the generator builds currentColor path fragments before writing the table.
stepNotes.3: ensureSpriteOnce handles SSR, absent body, and pre-existing sprite nodes, but its module boolean can stay true after the node is removed or the active document is replaced; recorded as Low.
stepNotes.4: Icon merges the remixicon class, forwards ordinary SVG props after its defaults, and renders a single use node; render-time sprite insertion is an idempotent but impure React-render advisory.
stepNotes.5: The innerHTML sink receives only statically imported generated path markup; runtime name values flow to React's href attribute and TypeScript constrains them to IconName, leaving no user-controlled HTML source.
stepNotes.6: The 109,438-byte sprite is parsed once through Object.entries/map/join and then shared by lightweight svg/use instances; the latch and React.memo bound repeat work.
stepNotes.7: Runtime ownership is clean and marker-free, but README.md names two different bun regeneration scripts and package.json defines neither; the generator's own node invocation is the working instruction.
stepNotes.8: UI TypeScript checking passed, while Vitest has no icon-specific file; SSR, adoption of an existing sprite, prop overrides, and stale-latch recovery therefore lack focused regression coverage.
stepNotes.9: Two Low findings were accepted (stale document latch and unusable regeneration commands), with render purity and missing tests advisory-only; no Critical item exists, so no reverify.md was created.
